analysis.title: U.S. Midterms: When Politics Misprices Fundamentals
key_insights: The midterms are a policy signal, not an endpoint. The outcome may show the direction, durability and practical constraints of future policy.
Political developments differ in investment significance within a sector, depending on competitive positioning, project or program funding, and exposure to regulatory change.
Voya's teams look to separate shifts in political expectations from policy changes that can meaningfully alter earnings and long-term economics.
Aerospace and defense: unified Democratic control of Congress could add uncertainty around defense appropriations, program timing and spending priorities.
Aerospace and defense: a split Congress could raise the risk of an extended Continuing Resolution to start CY2027, holding base defense funding near prior-year levels.

Aerospace and defense: a prolonged CR could delay new program starts and contract awards and push revenue or cash flow timing to the right. Multi-year frameworks help visibility only as they become funded contracts and production rates rise.

Aerospace and defense: programs backed by signed contracts, established backlogs or enduring mission priorities have less economic exposure than newer starts that depend on the next appropriations cycle. The opportunity may be greatest where the market discounts an intact program because of timing uncertainty.

Health care: the election may signal shifts in coverage, reimbursement, drug pricing and research funding, but direction and impact vary by subsector. Providers, managed care, biopharma and life science tools should not be treated as one political trade.

Health care: providers are exposed through coverage, utilization and uncompensated care. Managed care organizations are exposed through membership, reimbursement and medical costs. Biopharma is exposed through Medicare and Medicaid drug pricing. Life science tools face indirect R&D funding risk, and medtech depends partly on provider utilization.

Health care: broad headlines may move subsectors together despite different exposure. Life science tools face less direct risk, biopharma has limited downside beyond current drug-pricing law, and sweeping managed care proposals such as Medicare for All remain unlikely to be implemented.

AI infrastructure and data centers: the elections may show the strength and geographic reach of resistance tied to power costs, grid access, permitting, zoning, water use and community impact. These concerns cross party lines, so state and local outcomes may matter as much as the federal result.

AI infrastructure and data centers: greater resistance could raise development costs, reduce tax benefits, require on-site power, or delay interconnection and construction. Projects with secured power, approvals and local support should be less exposed than those still dependent on future grid capacity or political backing.

AI infrastructure and data centers: political constraints may increase the scarcity value of secured capacity and shift spending toward on-site power, microgrids, grid upgrades and connections between existing facilities.

The administration's industrial policy priorities, including national security, AI and domestic manufacturing, are likely to remain intact. The midterms may shape implementation rather than direction.
Bottom line: markets will trade the election, and Voya looks for the disconnects it creates. The result matters when policy expectations change the earnings path, not merely the political narrative.

sector_views.rationale: Temporary budget friction can create dispersion between delayed revenue and impaired demand. Programs with signed contracts or backlogs may be mispriced, while newer starts dependent on the next budget decision warrant more caution.
Policy affects subsectors differently. Opportunities arise when broad market reactions overstate the impact on a company's earnings and long-term fundamentals.

Secured power and approvals may gain scarcity value, while later-stage projects dependent on future grid capacity, permitting or incentives carry more risk. Spending may shift toward on-site power, microgrids and grid upgrades.

risk_factors: A split Congress could lead to an extended Continuing Resolution to start CY2027, delaying defense program starts and contract awards.
Unified Democratic control of Congress could add uncertainty around defense appropriations and spending priorities.
Local and state resistance to data centers over power costs, grid access, permitting, zoning and water use could raise costs, reduce tax benefits and delay construction.
Broad political headlines could pressure whole sectors regardless of company-level exposure.

tension_points.bull_case: Political noise may push prices away from fundamentals, so investors can find mispriced names where timing uncertainty is treated as impaired demand, such as defense programs with signed contracts or data center projects with secured power.
tension_points.bear_case: Newer defense programs dependent on the next appropriations cycle, and later-stage data center developments dependent on future grid capacity, permitting or incentives, face real economic risk from policy and local resistance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extended Continuing Resolution to start CY2027 that delays new program starts and awards would weigh on defense names that depend on the next appropriations cycle.

theme_stances.key_argument: Markets will trade the election on headlines, creating disconnects between political perception and company fundamentals.
theme_stances.evidence: Markets will trade the election. We look for the disconnects it creates.

theme_stances.key_argument: A split Congress could extend a Continuing Resolution into CY2027, delaying new program starts while sparing programs with signed contracts.
theme_stances.evidence: could raise the risk of an extended Continuing Resolution (CR) to start CY2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Power cost, grid access and permitting resistance crosses party lines and could raise costs for projects that still depend on future grid capacity.
theme_stances.evidence: state and local outcomes may prove as consequential as the federal result
